home.heroLine: Hand-pulled noodles. Lamb over charcoal. Tea first.

lagman.title: Laghman
lagman.text: A rope of wheat dough is stretched, folded and stretched again until it is as thin as string. Served with lamb, peppers, tomato and celery from the wok.

polo.title: Polo
polo.text: Rice, lamb, carrots and raisins cook together in the kazan until the rice has taken up the fat and the sweetness of the carrots.

kebab.title: Shish kebab
kebab.text: Cubed lamb, cumin, chili. Two minutes over the embers, then straight to the table.

manti.title: Manti
manti.text: Steamed dumplings with lamb and onion, six pieces, with yogurt. Each one closed by hand.

tea.title: Tea
tea.text: Saffron, rose buds, cardamom and goji in the pot. It reaches the table before the menu does.

home.roadText: Kashgar, Turpan and Ürümqi lie on the old Silk Road in western China. That is where the recipes, the spices and the pictures on our walls come from.
home.craftTitle: The dough is pulled when you order
home.craftText: Kneaded in the morning, rested until midday. Only with your order is the rope pulled and dropped into boiling water. It takes three minutes longer than noodles from a packet. You can taste it.
home.roomText: The fabrics on the columns are ikat from Xinjiang, the caps are called doppa. On the walls hang the Heytgah mosque in Kashgar, Ürümqi and Turpan.
home.bookText: Choose a date and number of guests, we do the rest. Confirmation by email, cancel up to two hours before.
home.sharingText: Dapanji for two to three, mixed grill for two, göshnan in wedges. From nine guests we put a menu together.

about.title: About us
about.lead: Karahan is a Uyghur restaurant in Winterthur. We cook what Uyghur families cook: noodles, lamb, vegetables, rice and tea.
about.whyText1: The Uyghurs live in Xinjiang in western China, on the old Silk Road. Their cooking joins noodles and wok from the east with pilaf, kebab and dumplings from Central Asia. It is halal, seasoned with cumin and chili, and uses a lot of fresh vegetables.
about.whyText2: In Switzerland this cuisine has hardly existed so far. The name Karahan goes back to the Karakhanids, a dynasty that ruled from Kashgar in the 10th century.

1.title: Dough
1.text: Laghman is pulled, manti and chüchüre are folded, samsa and göshnan are baked. Fresh every day.

2.title: Spices
2.text: Cumin and chili at the grill. Star anise, coriander and saffron in soups and tea.

3.title: Halal
3.text: Meat from halal-certified suppliers. No pork, no alcohol in the food.

4.title: At the table
4.text: Big plates go in the middle. Tea comes first.

kashgar.title: Kashgar
kashgar.text: Oasis city on the western edge of the Taklamakan desert. Known for the Heytgah mosque, the Sunday market and the tea houses. Laghman and samsa come from here.

urumqi.title: Ürümqi
urumqi.text: Capital of Xinjiang, at the foot of the Tianshan mountains. Dapanji, the big plate of chicken, is the city's best-known dish.

turpan.title: Turpan
turpan.text: An oasis 150 metres below sea level, the hottest region of China. Grapes, raisins, melons. The raisins in polo traditionally come from here.
